claims.text: Incorporating machine-learning potentials into ab initio molecular dynamics can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method is intended to treat both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems.
Machine-learning potentials will make the molecular-dynamics simulations more computationally efficient.
The proposed method will compute fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties faster than explicit ab initio workflows.
The proposed method will retain accuracy similar to explicit ab initio methods.
The relevant composition domain is high-entropy systems.
The relevant temperature domain is the high-temperature range associated with fusion properties.
A tenfold computational-cost reduction while keeping free-energy differences within 1% is the proposed success criterion.
